newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-DALLAS BURN WIN FIFTH STRAIGHT MLS GAMES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DALLAS BURN WIN FIFTH STRAIGHT MLS GAMES.

text.p: Swiss star Alain Sutter scored for the Dallas Burn, who defeated the Tampa Bay Mutiny 3-1 to win their fifth consecutive game in Major League Soccer action over the weekend.

Diego Sonora scored for the Western Conference leaders in the 37th minute before Sutter, who joined the Burn after transferring from SC Freiburg of the German Bundesliga, struck in the 52nd minute. Gerrel Elliott added an insurance goal for the Burn (7-4).

Roy Lassiter, last year's scoring champion, scored his second goal of the season for the Mutiny (5-4) before he left with a pulled hamstring. Defender Cle Kooiman was red-carded in the 58th minute for kicking Mexican Damian Alvarez in the back. Goalkeeper Mark Dodd made 10 saves for the Burn.

The slumping Mutiny then dropped a second game within 48 hours, losing to the New York/New Jersey MetroStars 3-2 Sunday night on a goal by U.S. international midfielder Mike Sorber in the 84th minute in East Rutherford, New Jersey. Donadoni scored a goal and set up another by Venezuelan native Giovanni Savarese for the MetroStars (5-6).
Colombian national team midfielder Carlos Valderrama created both of the Mutiny's goals off free kicks, by Alan Prampin and Giuseppe Galderisi.

The second-place Kansas City Wizards (5-4) stayed within striking distance of the Burn with a 3-1 win over the Columbus Crew (6-4) as Matt McKeon scored twice within a five-minute span midway through the first half in Kansas City, Missouri.
Mark Chung also scored for the winners before Peter Marino tallied for Columbus.

Bolivian international Jaime Moreno scored early and late to take his league-leading total to nine goals as D.C. United stopped the San Jose Clash 3-1 in Washington. El Salvadoran national team member Raul Diaz Arce also added a goal for United (7-3), which is in first place in the Eastern Conference.
U.S. international Eric Wynalda converted a penalty kick for the Clash (4-7) in the 77th minute.

Chinquinho Conde, captain of the Mozambique national team, scored his second goal of the game with three minutes remaining to lift the New England Revolution (6-4) to a 2-1 win over the Colorado Rapids (4-7) in Denver.
Jamaican Wolde Harris had given Colorado a 1-0 lead in the 12th minute before Conde equalised in the 36th.
